title: Zonal fallback condenser with staggered drain and SLO-lease throttling
author: Priya Menon
release_notes: Introduces a zonal fallback condenser for smoother cross-zone failovers, staggered drain to avoid thundering rebalances, and a SLO-lease based throttler to protect critical tenants during surges.
description:
Motivation: We observed rapid cross-zone failovers during multi-zone pressure events that caused cascading cold-starts and SLO violations for high-priority tenants. This PR implements a zonal fallback condenser that reduces the frequency and breadth of cross-zone failovers by batching zone-level fallback decisions and applying a staggered drain to minimize simultaneous capacity movement. It also introduces an SLO-lease throttler which enforces short-duration request admission caps tied to per-tenant SLO credit windows (linked to ENG-12988 and SRE-402).

Summary of changes: 1) Fallback condenser: a coordinator that aggregates zone health signals and defers non-critical fallbacks for a small, randomized window to allow transient oscillations to stabilize. 2) Staggered drain: when an instance is marked for eviction, churn is reduced by phased connection draining with jittered offsets per shard. 3) SLO-lease throttler: a lightweight token bucket keyed by tenant SLO slices; integrates with existing prioritizer so critical routes are preserved. 4) Observability: added new metrics (zonal_fallback_decisions, zonal_drain_phases, slo_lease_rejections) and tracing spans for decision flow. 5) Safety: conservative default config and a runtime flag to opt-in per-deployment.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc linked in PR: Linear ENG-12988 overview
- [x] Unit tests for condenser state machine and lease accounting
- [x] Integration tests exercising staggered drain under simulated multi-zone load
- [x] End-to-end performance run verifying no statistically significant increase in median latency for mainline requests
- [x] Telemetry dashboards and alerts defined

Implementation notes: The condenser lives in serving/controlplane/fallback and exposes a small API consumed by the scheduler. Decision commits are timestamped and deduplicated for a 30s window to avoid flip-flops. The staggered drain uses per-shard seed derived from instance id to compute phase offsets; offsets are bounded (default 2–8s) to prevent long drains. SLO-lease throttler attaches to admission middleware and consults a compact in-memory lease table; leases decay linearly and can be bumped by emergency overrides from ops.

Testing and validation: Local unit/integration tests included under serving/controlplane/fallback/tests and admission/tests. Simulation harness (benchmark-lab/failover-sim) was used to replay a 2-hour production incident trace with condenser on/off toggles; condenser reduced multi-zone failover frequency by ~62% and decreased the number of concurrent cold-starts by 48% in the replay. Canary rollout was executed on a single staging zone for 24h before broad rollout.

Rollout plan: Feature gated via runtime flag fallback.condenser.enabled=false by default. 1) Canary on staging for 24h. 2) Canary to 10% of production traffic for 6h with close monitoring of slo.requests_p50/p95 and zonal_fallback_decisions. 3) Gradual increase to 50% then full rollout if metrics stable. 4) If any of slo.requests_p95 or error.rate increase by >10% relative to baseline, auto-rollback trigger will disable the feature.

Backward compatibility and safety: The default behavior is no-op when the condenser is disabled. SLO-lease throttling respects existing tenant priority rules and cannot reject traffic for admin or emergency overrides. All new metrics are opt-in to APM billing to avoid surprise costs.

Related work: builds on prior rate-gating circuitry and soft-eviction orchestration (see ENG-11520 and SRE-288 references). This PR is intentionally conservative — it aims to reduce noisy cross-zone behavior without changing core routing logic.

Merging: Squash merge after approvals and green CI.

Notes on edge cases: We found a race when a node rings up after a condenser decision but before drain phases are committed; added a commit that reconciles phase state on rejoin. There is an acknowledged limitation where zone-wide simultaneous hardware replacement may still require manual intervention; documented in ops runbook.
